title: Pre-Analysis — Spherical Bearing and Heat Shield Window at the Auxiliary Power Unit Aft Mount
abstract: Re-analysis of the spherical bearing standard, opened to decide whether the heat shield window should be offered separately and delegated to the customer services organisation as a standalone option.

sections.objective: Establish whether the heat shield inspection window can be offered independently of the bearing conversion, and what has to be true for an aircraft to take one without the other.
sections.findings_summary: The question was delegated to customer services and the standalone option was recommended. The window is a cut in the heat shield and has no dependency on the mount standard at all; the only reason it was bundled with the bearing was that it was developed alongside it. Operators are asking for the access benefit now and the bearing is a twenty-four week lead item, so bundling costs them a year of inspection time for no engineering reason. Two items were confirmed. The cut must be made from the same template in both cases so that an aircraft taking the window first does not repeat the operation. The inspection task has to check for the window before it sends the engineer to drop the heat shield, and at the time of this analysis it did not.
sections.next_steps: Delegate the standalone window offering to customer services. Add the window check to the inspection task before the heat shield drop step. Confirm the template is a shared tooling item so that both bulletins reference the same reference.

tasks.title: Establish whether the window has any dependency on the mount standard
Check the inspection task access route

expected_findings.rationale: The task sends the engineer to drop the aft heat shield without first checking whether the inspection window is fitted, which wastes six hours on every converted aircraft.
expected_findings.resolution: Add the window check before the heat shield drop step.

expected_findings.rationale: If the window is offered separately, the bearing bulletin has to skip its own window step on an aircraft that already has one, and both must cut from the same template so the resulting shield is identical.
expected_findings.resolution: Add the skip condition and confirm the template is a shared tooling reference.

evidence.similarity_note: The crew procedure describes the cooling run-on before shutdown in operational terms and shares no identifier with the mount work, but the run-on is what sets the thermal cycle the mount sees.

expected_findings.rationale: The mount inspection interval assumes an average thermal cycle count, which depends on how often the unit is shut down with the run-on completed. The crew procedure was checked to confirm it does not permit a shortened run-on.
expected_findings.resolution: No change. The procedure requires the full run-on.

expected_non_findings.reason: Same ATA 6D and the same mount, and it also adds an inspection access feature, but it did not exist at the time of this analysis and its borescope port is a separate cut in a different panel.

type_data.conclusion: Standalone window option recommended and delegated to customer services.
